mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-01.prompt: When the letters of the alphabet are assigned their integer values (A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, …, Z = 26), the word-product of a sequence of letters is the product of the letter-values of its letters. When the square root of JULY's word-product is put into its simplest radical form of $a\sqrt{b}$, where $b$ has no perfect-square factors greater than 1, what is the value of $b$?

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-02.prompt: When the letters of the alphabet are assigned their integer values (A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, …, Z = 26), the word-product of a sequence of letters is the product of the letter-values of its letters. What sequence of letters has the same word-product as JULY, but (1) does not contain any of the letters in JULY, (2) contains the letter N, (3) does not contain any of its letters more than once and (4) has its letters in alphabetical order?

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-03.prompt: When the letters of the alphabet are assigned their integer values (A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, …, Z = 26), the word-sum of a sequence of letters is the sum of the letter-values of its letters. The values of the letters of a particular four-letter sequence form an arithmetic sequence and this sequence has the same word-sum as JULY. What is the least possible value of a letter in this four-letter sequence?
